purpose: deploy the release candidate to staging and prove it behaves as it will in production before approval
entry_criteria: Release candidate has an immutable artifact digest
Staging mirrors production configuration closely enough to be meaningful
procedure: Deploy the exact artifact that would go to production, using the same pipeline and steps.
Apply database migrations to staging first and record duration and result.
Run smoke, integration and critical-journey tests against staging.
Compare configuration, versions and data shape with production and list known differences.
Record results and any defects; block promotion on critical failures.
Hand the evidence and the list of differences to release readiness (stage 128).
acceptance_criteria: Staging runs the exact production candidate digest
Critical journeys passed or defects block promotion
validation_method: Change authority approval and post-deploy verification.

validation.command: kubectl get deployment app -n staging -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'   # example
validation.expect: image digest equals the release candidate digest

validation.check: complete the critical journeys on staging with a test account

failure_modes.mode: A different build was deployed to staging
Staging differs from production in ways that matter
failure_modes.response: Fix the difference or record the risk for the approver

failure_modes.mode: Migration works only on tiny data
failure_modes.detection: Staging data is far smaller than production

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: Release candidate digest sha256:ab12 is deployed to staging by the same pipeline. The migration takes 40 seconds, the critical journeys pass, and the only known difference is a smaller database.
